questions.q:
If speed (V), acceleration (A) and force (F) are considered

as fundamental units, the dimension of Young's modulus

will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let [Y] = [V] $^{a}[\mathrm{~F}]^{\mathrm{b}}[\mathrm{A}]^{\mathrm{c}}\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-1}\right]^{\mathrm{a}}\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]^{\mathrm{b}}\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-2}\right]^{\mathrm{c}}\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{M}^{b} \mathrm{~L}^{\mathrm{a}+b+\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{T}^{-\mathrm{a}-2 \mathrm{~b}-2 \mathrm{c}}\right]$

Comparing power both side of similar terms we get,

$b=1, a+b+c=-1,-a-2 b-2 c=-2$

solving above equations we get

$a=-4, b=1, c=2$

so $[\mathrm{Y}]=\left[\mathrm{V}^{-4} \mathrm{FA}^{2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{V}^{-4} \mathrm{~A}^{2} \mathrm{~F}\right]$

questions.q: In the equation X+aY2[Y-b]=RT, X is pressure, Y is volume, R is universal gas constant and T is temperature. The physical quantity equivalent to the ratio ab is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
X & aY2 have the same dimensions. Y & b also have the same dimensions.

Therefore,

aY2=ML-1T-2⇒a=ML-1T-2×L6=ML5T-2

and b=L3.

So, the dimensions of ab is,

ab=ML5T-2L3=ML2T-2.

This is the dimensional form of energy. Hence, this is the right option.
